title: Indonesia | APU PPT PPPSPM Programme under POJK 8/2023
tagline: Apply Law 8/2010, Law 9/2013 and OJK's POJK 8/2023: CDD, PEPs, PPATK reporting on goAML, DTTOT freezing and the bank's programme.
description:
This quest teaches Indonesia's own rules on anti-money laundering (APU), countering the financing of terrorism (PPT) and preventing the financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction (PPPSPM) for conventional banks.

It is based on **Law 8/2010** on money laundering, **Law 9/2013** on terrorism financing, **OJK Regulation (POJK) 8/2023**, OJK's freezing guidance and **PPATK**'s reporting guidance for goAML. POJK 8/2023 requires banks to train officers and staff at least once a year, and directors must make sure staff in relevant units and new joiners attend; this quest is built for that yearly and induction training.

You will learn the offences and penalties, CDD, beneficial owners, PEPs and EDD, suspicious, cash and cross-border reports to PPATK, tipping off, immediate freezing under the DTTOT and DPPSPM, records, staff screening and OJK's sanctions.

The quest builds knowledge; it does not replace your bank's own policies, procedures or legal advice. Always follow your institution's approved procedures and the current official texts.
audience: Branch, teller, customer service and account-opening staff at conventional banks in Indonesia
AML/CFT/CPF unit, transaction monitoring and list-screening staff who analyse alerts and file reports to PPATK
Relationship managers, payments, treasury and correspondent banking staff
New joiners who need AML/CFT/CPF training under POJK 8/2023
Directors, commissioners, internal auditors and risk managers who oversee the programme
outcomes: Explain the offences, penalties and tipping-off ban in Law 8/2010 and Law 9/2013
Apply POJK 8/2023 CDD, beneficial owner, PEP and EDD requirements
Recognise suspicious transactions and meet PPATK reporting deadlines for LTKM, LTKT and LTKL through goAML
Freeze and report correctly when a customer matches the DTTOT or DPPSPM
Describe the five pillars of the bank's programme, staff screening and yearly training duties
Describe OJK's administrative sanctions and how to avoid them

quest.name: The Nusantara Shield Mission
quest.premise: You have just joined the AML/CFT/CPF unit of Bank Lintas Samudra, a fictional conventional bank with branches from Medan to Denpasar. Over five stages you will learn Indonesia's laws, protect the bank's door, report to PPATK, freeze terrorist and proliferation funds, and get the programme ready for OJK's examiners.

badge.description: Awarded for mastering Indonesia's AML, CFT and CPF rules for conventional banks under Law 8/2010, Law 9/2013 and POJK 8/2023.

cast.name: Dewi Kartika
cast.role: Head of the AML/CFT/CPF unit, Jakarta, your mentor

sessions.title: The Framework: Laws, Offences and Who's Who
sessions.summary: Map Indonesia's AML/CFT/CPF rulebook: Law 8/2010, Law 9/2013, POJK 8/2023, the roles of OJK and PPATK, the laundering offences and their penalties.
objectives: Explain how Law 8/2010, Law 9/2013 and POJK 8/2023 fit together
Distinguish active and passive laundering under Law 8/2010 and their maximum penalties
Describe the roles of OJK, PPATK and the bank
Respond to customer questions about reporting without tipping off

cards.title: Day one at Bank Lintas Samudra
cards.setting: AML/CFT/CPF unit, Bank Lintas Samudra head office, Jalan Jenderal Sudirman, Jakarta. 8:45 am.

lines.text: Your badge reads: AML/CFT/CPF Officer. Your quest: keep criminal proceeds, terrorist funds and proliferation money out of Bank Lintas Samudra, a fictional conventional commercial bank with branches from Medan to Denpasar.
Selamat datang! I'm Dewi Kartika, head of the bank's special AML/CFT/CPF unit. Five stages lie ahead of you, and OJK's supervisors visit us next quarter.
Rizal Hakim, transaction monitoring. Medan has already called. A trader brought in a large bag of cash and asked our teller a strange question.
(on video from Medan) Maria Simanjuntak, branch manager. He asked whether deposits 'just under the limit' get reported to the government. My teller froze.
So which rule applies? The money laundering law? OJK's regulation? PPATK's reporting rules? The teller wants a one-line answer.
There is no one-line answer, which is why we start here. Before you judge a single deposit, you need the map: the laws, the offences and who does what.
Agus Wibowo, the director who oversees compliance. Stage one is the Statute Gate. Learn the rulebook the way an OJK examiner reads it.

cards.title: Indonesia's AML/CFT/CPF rulebook in five layers

scenes.heading: Law 8/2010 sets the base
scenes.narration: Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2010, the law on preventing and eradicating money laundering, creates the laundering offences, names the reporting parties, including banks, and sets their reporting duties.

scenes.heading: Law 9/2013 covers terror funds
scenes.narration: Undang-Undang Nomor 9 Tahun 2013 makes terrorism financing a crime, adds its own reporting and tipping-off rules, and creates the domestic terrorist list with immediate freezing.

scenes.heading: OJK writes the bank rules
scenes.narration: For banks, OJK is the supervisory and regulatory authority. Its regulation POJK 8/2023, in force since 14 June 2023, sets the programme every bank must run against laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

scenes.heading: PPATK receives the reports
scenes.narration: PPATK, the Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre, is the financial intelligence unit. Banks file their reports to it electronically through the goAML application.

scenes.heading: Your bank fills in the detail
scenes.narration: Finally, the bank turns all of this into written policies and procedures, proposed by the directors and approved by the Board of Commissioners. That is what you apply every day.

cards.title: From statute to your desk
cards.caption: Higher layers bind lower ones: a bank procedure can be stricter than POJK 8/2023, never looser.

items.label: Laws 8/2010 and 9/2013
items.detail: Offences, reporting parties, reporting duties, tipping off, freezing and criminal penalties.

items.label: POJK 8/2023 (OJK)
items.detail: The bank's programme: five pillars, CDD, EDD, lists, records, training and administrative sanctions.

items.label: PPATK reporting rules
items.detail: How and when reports are filed through goAML, plus PPATK guidance on spotting suspicion.

items.label: Bank policies and procedures
items.detail: Written, approved by the Board of Commissioners, reviewed every year and applied consistently.

cards.title: Decode the acronyms
cards.prompt: Indonesian AML vocabulary is full of acronyms. Match each one to its meaning.

pairs.right: Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme: countering the financing of terrorism
Preventing the financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction
Indonesia's financial intelligence unit, which receives and analyses reports
Laporan Transaksi Keuangan Mencurigakan: the suspicious transaction report
The domestic list of suspected terrorists and terrorist organisations

cards.question: Maria's trader worries about reports 'to the government'. Which body actually receives a bank's suspicious transaction reports?
options: PPATK, the financial intelligence unit
OJK, the bank's supervisor
Bank Indonesia, the central bank
The Indonesian National Police
cards.explanation: Law 8/2010 requires banks to send suspicious, large cash and cross-border transfer reports to PPATK. OJK supervises whether the bank complies, and the police investigate cases PPATK passes on, but the report itself goes to PPATK.

cards.title: Three ways to launder under Law 8/2010
cards.body:
Law 8/2010 has three core laundering offences:

- **Article 3 (active):** placing, transferring, spending, paying, converting or moving assets abroad that you know or should reasonably suspect are criminal proceeds, in order to hide their origin. Up to **20 years** in prison and a fine of up to **IDR 10 billion**.
- **Article 4 (concealing):** hiding the true origin, source, location, use or ownership of such assets. Up to **20 years** and **IDR 5 billion**.
- **Article 5 (passive):** receiving or controlling such assets, for example as a deposit, gift or payment. Up to **5 years** and **IDR 1 billion**. This does not apply to a reporting party that meets its reporting duties.

**Proceeds** come from a long list of crimes, including corruption, bribery, narcotics, fraud, tax, banking and forestry crimes, plus any crime punishable by four years or more, whether committed in Indonesia or abroad, if it is also a crime under Indonesian law.

cards.title: Active or passive laundering?
cards.prompt: Decide which group of Law 8/2010 offences fits each person's conduct.

items.text: A trader converts bribe money into US dollars and wires it abroad to hide where it came from
A cousin registers a villa bought with drug money in his own name to hide the real owner
A friend accepts a car as a gift although he should have suspected it was bought with fraud proceeds
A nominee lets a corruption suspect park funds in her account, knowing their source
An official buys gold bars with embezzled funds so the money can no longer be traced
A shop owner takes payment he suspects comes from illegal logging

cards.title: Maximum criminal penalties
cards.caption: Figures are the statutory maxima in Law 8/2010; a court sets the actual sentence.

items.label: Article 3: active laundering
items.detail: Prison and fine maxima for placing, transferring or converting proceeds to hide their origin.

items.label: Article 4: concealment
items.detail: Hiding the origin, location or true ownership of proceeds.

items.label: Article 5: passive laundering
items.detail: Receiving or controlling proceeds; reporting parties doing their duty are exempt.

items.label: Corporations (Article 7)
items.detail: Maximum fine, plus possible extra penalties such as licence revocation or dissolution.

items.label: Tipping off (Article 12)
items.detail: For directors, commissioners or staff who reveal an STR to the customer or others.

cards.title: A second visit in Medan
cards.setting: Bank Lintas Samudra, Medan branch. The next morning.

lines.text: He's back. Pak Hendra, a palm oil trader. Yesterday IDR 480 million in cash. Today he wants to deposit another IDR 450 million, split across his wife's and his son's accounts.
Separate days, separate accounts, each amount below the cash reporting line. And yesterday he asked what gets reported.
His documents are in order and he's a long-standing customer. My teller doesn't want to offend him.
Remember how Law 8/2010 defines a suspicious transaction. One of its limbs covers transactions that seem designed to avoid a report the bank must file.
Then the question is not whether he's a nice man. It's what the teller does in the next five minutes.

cards.title: Five minutes at the counter
cards.situation: Pak Hendra is at the teller window with IDR 450 million in cash for two family accounts. He smiles and asks: 'These smaller amounts don't go to PPATK, do they?' The teller calls Maria over. The bank has not yet filed anything on him. What should Maria do?

choices.text: Explain the IDR 500 million cash-report threshold so he can plan his deposits without trouble
choices.outcome: This hands the customer a map for avoiding reports. Helping someone stay under a reporting line can itself feed suspicion and exposes staff to serious consequences. Staff should never coach customers around reporting duties.

choices.text: Carry out the CDD the transaction requires, avoid any discussion of reporting, note his words and escalate to the AML unit
choices.outcome: Correct. The amount alone triggers CDD under POJK 8/2023, and his question plus the split deposits may point to avoidance of reporting. Maria records the facts and reports internally; the AML unit decides whether an LTKM goes to PPATK. She says nothing about reports.

choices.text: Tell him firmly that the bank will now report him to PPATK as suspicious
choices.outcome: This is tipping off. Law 8/2010 bars directors, commissioners and staff from telling a customer about an STR being prepared or filed, with penalties of up to 5 years and IDR 1 billion. It also warns a possible launderer.

choices.text: Process the deposits and wait a few weeks to see whether he keeps splitting cash before telling anyone
choices.outcome: Partly right: monitoring matters. But his question and the pattern are already worth escalating now. Waiting delays the analysis the AML unit must do, and the three-working-day STR clock starts once the bank knows of suspicious elements.

cards.title: Words an examiner expects you to know

cards.back: Reporting party: any person or business that Law 8/2010 requires to report to PPATK. Banks are listed first among financial service providers.
Supervisory and regulatory authority. For banks this is OJK, which sets KYC rules and supervises compliance.
'Should reasonably have suspected'. The laundering offences do not require certainty: what a reasonable person would have suspected can be enough.
Controlling personnel of a corporation: people who set or carry out its policy without needing a superior's approval. They can be punished along with the company.
Suspicious financial transaction, defined in Law 8/2010 in four limbs (you will meet them in stage three).
Assets of any kind, movable or immovable, tangible or intangible, obtained directly or indirectly.

items.label: Law 8/2010 enacted
items.detail: New money laundering law; PPATK confirmed as the independent FIU.

items.label: Law 9/2013 enacted
items.detail: Terrorism financing offence, TF reporting and the DTTOT freezing regime.

items.label: FATF observer
items.detail: Indonesia admitted as an observer to the Financial Action Task Force.

items.label: POJK 8/2023 in force
items.detail: Replaces OJK's 2017 regulation and adds proliferation financing.

items.label: FATF full member

cards.question: A company is convicted of laundering under Law 8/2010. Who can be punished?
options: Only the employee who handled the money
Only the company, never individuals
The company and/or its controlling personnel
Only directors named in the articles of association
cards.explanation: Article 6 of Law 8/2010 allows penalties against the corporation and/or its controlling personnel when the laundering was ordered by them, served the company's purposes, fell within the offender's role and was meant to benefit the company.

cards.title: Real case: Indonesia joins the FATF (PPATK, 2023)
cards.body:
PPATK announced that on **25 October 2023**, at the FATF plenary in Paris, Indonesia was accepted by acclamation as the FATF's **40th member**.

The road was long. Indonesia had been an observer since **29 June 2018** and then went through a mutual evaluation testing both its laws and how well they work. In February 2023 the FATF gave Indonesia a fast-track action plan focused on three outcomes: **supervision of compliance**, **asset confiscation** and **proliferation financing**. PPATK reported that all **48 action items** were completed.

**What it means for you:** membership is judged on effectiveness, not paperwork. Examiners now look for real outcomes inside banks: useful suspicious transaction reports, working list screening and staff who know their role. Every LTKM you help write feeds Indonesia's results.

cards.title: When a customer asks 'who sees my reports?'
cards.body:
- Do not confirm or deny that any report exists or will exist.
- Do not explain thresholds so the customer can plan around them.
- Use a neutral line: *'We follow the bank's standard procedures for all customers.'*
- Write down the exact words, time and context straight after the conversation.
- Escalate through the internal channel to the AML unit the same day.

cards.title: Stage one: what to remember
items: Law 8/2010 creates the laundering offences and the reporting duties of banks; Law 9/2013 does the same for terrorism financing.
POJK 8/2023, in force since 14 June 2023, is OJK's rulebook for the bank's AML, CFT and CPF programme.
PPATK is the FIU and receives reports; OJK supervises the bank and imposes administrative sanctions.
Laundering can be active (Articles 3 and 4) or passive (Article 5); 'should reasonably have suspected' can be enough.
Penalties reach 20 years in prison, and corporations face fines of up to IDR 100 billion.
Never tip off: telling a customer about an STR is a crime for staff, directors and commissioners.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time a customer asked you an unusual question about limits, reports or 'the government'. How did you answer, and what would you write down now?

quiz.question: Which institution serves as Indonesia's financial intelligence unit?
options: PPATK
OJK
Bank Indonesia
The Directorate General of Taxes
quiz.explanation: Law 8/2010 establishes PPATK as the independent body that receives and analyses reports. OJK is the banks' supervisor, not the FIU.

quiz.question: What is the maximum prison term for active laundering under Article 3 of Law 8/2010?
options: 5 years
15 years
10 years
20 years
quiz.explanation: Article 3 carries up to 20 years in prison and a fine of up to IDR 10 billion. Five years is the cap for passive laundering under Article 5.

quiz.question: Budi accepts a new car from a friend as a gift. He had good reason to suspect it was bought with fraud proceeds but did not hide anything. Which offence is most relevant?
options: Active laundering under Article 3, up to 20 years and IDR 10 billion
No offence, because Budi did not know for certain where the money came from
Passive laundering under Article 5, up to 5 years and IDR 1 billion
Concealment under Article 4, up to 20 years and IDR 5 billion
quiz.explanation: Receiving or controlling assets one knows or should reasonably suspect are proceeds is passive laundering under Article 5. Certainty is not required, so 'no offence' is wrong.

quiz.question: Which knowledge standard do the laundering offences in Law 8/2010 use?
options: The person must have been convicted of the predicate crime first
The prosecution must prove the person planned the predicate crime
The person must have admitted knowing where the money came from
The person knew or should reasonably have suspected the assets were proceeds of crime
quiz.explanation: Articles 3 to 5 apply to assets the person knew or should reasonably have suspected ('patut diduga') were proceeds. The other options add requirements the law does not state.

quiz.question: Proceeds of a fraud committed in Singapore are moved through an Indonesian account to hide their origin. When can this be laundering under Law 8/2010?
options: Only if the fraud was committed by an Indonesian citizen
Never, because predicate crimes must take place in Indonesia
When the fraud is also a crime under Indonesian law
Only if Singapore asks Indonesia to prosecute
quiz.explanation: Law 8/2010 covers proceeds of listed crimes committed inside or outside Indonesia, provided the act is also a crime under Indonesian law. Nationality and a foreign request are not conditions.

quiz.question: Which authority issued POJK 8/2023 and supervises how banks apply their AML, CFT and CPF programme?
options: OJK (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan)
PPATK, the financial intelligence unit
Bank Indonesia's payment system department
The Ministry of Finance
quiz.explanation: POJK stands for Peraturan OJK, a regulation of the Financial Services Authority, which is the supervisory and regulatory authority for banks under Law 8/2010.

quiz.question: What is the maximum principal fine for a corporation convicted of laundering under Law 8/2010?
options: IDR 10 billion
IDR 1 billion
IDR 25 billion
IDR 100 billion
quiz.explanation: Article 7 sets a maximum fine of IDR 100 billion for corporations, plus possible extra penalties such as announcement of the verdict, freezing of business or revocation of licence. IDR 10 billion is the cap for individuals under Article 3.

quiz.question: What did POJK 8/2023 add compared with the 2017 OJK regulation it replaced?
options: Prevention of proliferation financing of weapons of mass destruction
The first rules on customer due diligence
The creation of PPATK as the FIU
Criminal penalties for money laundering
quiz.explanation: POJK 8/2023 extended the programme to proliferation financing (PPPSPM). CDD rules existed before, PPATK was created by statute, and criminal penalties sit in the laws, not in an OJK regulation.

quiz.question: A bank employee tells a customer that an STR about him is being drafted. What penalty does Law 8/2010 allow?
options: Up to 5 years in prison and a fine of up to IDR 1 billion
Only an internal warning letter from the bank
Up to 20 years in prison and a fine of up to IDR 10 billion
An administrative fine imposed by OJK only
quiz.explanation: Article 12 bars directors, commissioners and staff of reporting parties from disclosing an STR in preparation or filed, and sets up to 5 years and IDR 1 billion for breaches.

quiz.question: A teller accepts a deposit, finds it suspicious and the bank reports it to PPATK as the law requires. Why is the teller not guilty of passive laundering under Article 5?
options: Tellers are not 'persons' under Law 8/2010
Article 5 expressly does not apply to reporting parties carrying out their reporting duties
Passive laundering only applies to amounts above IDR 500 million
The teller is protected only if OJK approves the deposit in advance
quiz.explanation: Article 5(2) excludes reporting parties that fulfil their reporting duties. There is no amount threshold for the offence and no OJK pre-approval mechanism.

sessions.title: Customer Due Diligence, Beneficial Owners and PEPs
sessions.summary: Apply POJK 8/2023 at the door and after it: CDD triggers, verification channels, beneficial owners, high-risk customers, PEPs, simplified CDD and refusals.
objectives: Recognise the five situations that trigger CDD
Identify beneficial owners of companies and trusts
Apply EDD and senior approval to PEPs, their families and close associates
Know when to refuse, close and report a relationship

cards.title: Two new accounts in Medan
cards.setting: Bank Lintas Samudra, Medan branch, corporate desk. 10:20 am.

lines.text: Busy morning! PT Sawit Makmur Abadi wants a corporate current account, and Ibu Ratna, wife of a regional head in North Sumatra, wants our premium savings package.
The company's director signed everything, but the share register shows a holding company in another country. Who actually owns it?
And Ibu Ratna's relationship manager is thrilled. She plans to move a large deposit next week.
Two classic tests for POJK 8/2023: the beneficial owner behind a company, and a politically exposed person's family member.
Neither is a reason to refuse business. Both are reasons to do the work properly before we say yes.
Stage two is the Gatehouse. Let's learn exactly what OJK expects at the door and after it.

scenes.heading: A new relationship
scenes.narration: POJK 8/2023 requires customer due diligence whenever the bank opens a business relationship with a prospective customer.

scenes.heading: IDR 100 million or more
scenes.narration: CDD is also needed for any transaction, in rupiah or foreign currency, worth at least IDR 100 million or its equivalent, including for walk-in customers.

scenes.heading: Fund transfers
scenes.narration: Every fund transfer transaction triggers CDD, whatever the amount.

scenes.heading: Signs of suspicion
scenes.narration: When there are indications of a suspicious transaction linked to laundering, terrorism financing or proliferation financing, CDD applies.

scenes.heading: Doubtful information
scenes.narration: Finally, if the bank doubts information given by the customer, a walk-in customer, an attorney or a beneficial owner, it must carry out CDD again.

items.label: Classify the customer
items.detail: Individual, corporation or legal arrangement such as a trust.

items.label: Identify
items.detail: Collect identity data, source of funds, income or net worth and purpose.

items.label: Verify
items.detail: In person, face to face by video, or non face to face with strong authentication.

items.label: Find the beneficial owner
items.detail: Acting for themselves or someone else? Identify and verify the real owner.

items.label: Rate the risk
items.detail: Group by risk level using identity, business, ownership, products and channels.

items.label: Approve or apply EDD
items.detail: High-risk customers and PEPs get enhanced due diligence and senior approval.

items.label: Monitor and update
items.detail: Check transactions against the profile and refresh data when things change.

cards.question: A walk-in customer with no account wants to buy a cashier's cheque for IDR 150 million. Does POJK 8/2023 require CDD?
options: No, CDD applies only to account holders
Yes, because the transaction is at least IDR 100 million
No, because walk-in customers are covered by simplified CDD
Only if the customer pays in cash rather than by transfer
cards.explanation: Article 19 of POJK 8/2023 requires CDD for transactions of IDR 100 million or more, and the regulation applies CDD to walk-in customers (WIC) as well as account holders. The payment method does not change that.

cards.title: CDD, EDD or refuse?
cards.prompt: Using POJK 8/2023, decide what the bank must do in each situation.

items.text: A salaried teacher opens a savings account with a valid ID and a clear purpose
A former minister of another country opens an investment account
A company whose owners are in a country the FATF has called for countermeasures against
An applicant asks to open an account under a made-up name
A customer refuses to say who the money really belongs to and the bank cannot establish the beneficial owner
A local shop owner deposits cash in line with her known turnover
A business partner of a domestic PEP asks to open a high-value account
A prospective customer appears on the DTTOT

cards.title: Verifying identity remotely
cards.caption: Physical face-to-face meetings remain the third option. Whatever the channel, the bank owns the result.

items.label: How it works
items.left: A real-time online meeting between bank staff and the applicant
items.right: No live meeting; the system checks identity electronically

items.label: Identity check
items.left: Staff compare the person, data and documents live
items.right: Uses national population data plus at least two authentication factors

items.label: Authentication
items.right: Something you are (biometric) and something you have; 'something you know' optional

items.label: Third-party tools
items.left: Allowed with a written agreement; the bank stays responsible
items.right: Same: provider must meet OJK criteria; data belongs to the bank

cards.title: Beneficial owners: who really stands behind the account
cards.body:
POJK 8/2023 defines the **beneficial owner** as the individual who ultimately owns the funds, controls the customer's transactions, gives the authority to transact, or controls a company or legal arrangement.

What the bank must do:
- **Ask the question every time:** is the customer acting for itself or for someone else?
- **Apply CDD or EDD to the beneficial owner**; if the owner is a PEP, EDD is required.
- **Use the higher risk:** if the customer and its owner have different risk levels, CDD follows the higher one.
- **For companies:** identify and verify owners from reliable sources. If in doubt, or nobody controls through ownership, find who controls by other means; if still nobody, identify the relevant director.
- **For trusts:** settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiaries and anyone who controls the trust.
- **If the beneficial owner cannot be established, refuse** the relationship or transaction.

cards.title: Finding the owner behind PT Sawit Makmur Abadi
cards.prompt: Put the bank's steps for a corporate customer in the order POJK 8/2023 implies.
steps: Classify the customer as a corporation and collect its identity data and documents
Ask whether the company acts for itself or on behalf of someone else
Trace who owns the company, through the foreign holding company if necessary
If ownership gives no clear answer, identify who controls the company by other means
If no individual can be found that way, identify the relevant director
Verify the beneficial owner's identity from reliable sources and apply CDD or EDD at the higher risk level

cards.title: The regional head's wife
cards.setting: Medan branch, relationship manager's office. 2:00 pm.

lines.text: Ibu Ratna is charming and her deposit would make our quarterly target. Her husband is a regional head, but the account is in her name only.
POJK 8/2023 covers PEPs' family members and close associates too. The same high-risk rules apply to them.
Do we need head office sign-off? She wants to start tomorrow.
A designated senior officer must approve. And we need to understand the source of funds and source of wealth, not just fill in a form.

cards.title: Opening for a PEP's family member
cards.situation: Ibu Ratna's relationship manager has her ID, tax number and a signed form stating 'family savings' as the source of funds. She plans to deposit IDR 3 billion next week. The RM wants to open the account today and 'tidy up the PEP paperwork later'. What should Maria do?

choices.text: Open the account today as the RM suggests, since the account is in the wife's name rather than the official's
choices.outcome: The rule follows the person, not the account title. POJK 8/2023 applies the high-risk treatment to PEPs' family members and close associates. Opening first and approving later breaks the senior-approval requirement.

choices.text: Treat her as PEP-related: get the designated senior officer's approval, analyse source of funds and wealth, then open with closer monitoring
choices.outcome: Correct. For PEPs, and for their family and close associates, the bank needs a designated senior officer's approval to open or continue, EDD that analyses source of funds and wealth, and stricter monitoring. It also records her in the separate high-risk customer list.

choices.text: Refuse the account because politically exposed people are too risky for the bank
choices.outcome: POJK 8/2023 does not ban PEPs. It requires enhanced measures. A blanket refusal is not what the rule asks for, although the senior officer may decline after EDD if the risk cannot be managed.

choices.text: Open the account but cap deposits below IDR 100 million until the paperwork is done
choices.outcome: This designs the relationship around a CDD trigger instead of applying EDD. The PEP link already requires approval and EDD before opening, whatever the deposit size.

cards.back: Someone entrusted with a prominent function, not middle or junior ranks: heads of state or government, senior politicians, officials, military or law enforcement officers, senior SOE executives, key party officials.
Foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and people with prominent functions in international organisations, such as directors, deputy directors and board members.
The bank must apply the same high-risk treatment to a PEP's family members and close associates.
A senior officer designated by the bank, who may approve, refuse, continue or end the relationship.
Periodic EDD, at least analysis of information on the customer or beneficial owner, the source of funds and the source of wealth.
Stricter monitoring of the relationship, and inclusion in the bank's separate list of high-risk customers.

cards.title: Keeping the profile alive
cards.caption: Articles 51 and 52 of POJK 8/2023 turn CDD into a continuous process, not a one-off form.

items.label: Monitor transactions
items.detail: Do they fit the customer's business, risk profile and source of funds?

items.label: Spot the mismatch
items.detail: Analyse every transaction that departs from the profile or usual pattern.

items.label: Ask carefully
items.detail: The bank may ask the customer about background and purpose, minding tipping off.

items.label: Update and document
items.detail: Refresh data and documents; directors approve the data-updating plan and results.

items.label: Re-rate or report
items.detail: Adjust the risk level; if the explanation is unconvincing, file an LTKM.

cards.question: A corporate customer is rated medium risk, but its beneficial owner is rated high risk. How should the bank apply due diligence?
options: Apply CDD or EDD based on the higher risk level
Average the two ratings to medium-high
Use the customer's rating, since the company holds the account
Use the owner's rating only if the owner signs the forms
cards.explanation: Article 32 of POJK 8/2023 says that where the risk levels of the customer and its beneficial owner differ, CDD or EDD follows the higher risk level.

cards.title: Real case: dormant accounts and account trading (PPATK, 2025)
cards.body:
In a press release of **18 May 2025**, PPATK said that in **2024** more than **28,000 accounts** obtained through the **buying and selling of bank accounts** had been used for online gambling deposits. Accounts held in other people's names were also widely used to collect proceeds of fraud, drug trafficking and other crimes.

Using its powers under Law 8/2010, PPATK temporarily halted transactions on accounts the banks' own data showed as **dormant**, explaining that dormant accounts controlled by third parties were a common route for abuse. Customers kept full rights to their funds and could ask their branch to reactivate the account.

**The CDD lesson:** an account in one person's name may be run by another. That is exactly why POJK 8/2023 makes the bank ask whether the customer acts for itself or for a beneficial owner, and keep checking the account's activity against the profile.

cards.title: Simplified CDD is not 'no CDD'
Stage two: what to remember
items: CDD is required for new relationships, transactions of IDR 100 million or more, fund transfers, suspicion and doubtful information.
Anonymous accounts and accounts in fictitious names are banned; refuse or close when CDD fails, documents look false or the customer is listed.
Always ask who the beneficial owner is; if it cannot be established, refuse the relationship.
PEPs, their families and close associates need a designated senior officer's approval, source of funds and wealth analysis and closer monitoring.
When a relationship is refused or closed for these reasons, the bank documents it and reports it to PPATK as suspicious.

cards.prompt: Pick one customer type you handle often. What would make you ask 'who really owns this money?', and how would you check the answer?

quiz.question: Which of these transactions triggers CDD under POJK 8/2023 regardless of its amount?
options: A cash deposit of IDR 50 million
A balance enquiry at an ATM
A fund transfer
A request for a printed account statement
quiz.explanation: Article 19 lists fund transfers as a CDD trigger without any amount. Cash transactions trigger CDD from IDR 100 million, and enquiries are not transactions.

quiz.question: Under POJK 8/2023, which pair of authentication factors must at least be used for non face-to-face electronic verification?
options: Something the applicant knows and a signed form
A password and a security question
Something the applicant is and something the applicant has
A selfie and a scanned utility bill only
quiz.explanation: Article 21 requires the use of population data and at least two factors: something you are and something you have. 'Something you know' can be added.

quiz.question: A corporate customer's ownership is spread so widely that no individual controls it through shares. What does POJK 8/2023 require next?
options: Record the beneficial owner as 'not applicable' and proceed
Refuse the company because it has no beneficial owner
Identify the individual who controls the company by other means, and failing that the relevant director
Accept the company's own statement that it has no owner
quiz.explanation: Article 33 says that if ownership gives no answer, the bank identifies who controls by other means; if there is still nobody, it identifies the relevant director. 'Not applicable' and automatic refusal are not the rule.

quiz.question: Which of these is a duty for PEP relationships under POJK 8/2023?
options: Approval from a designated senior officer to open or continue the relationship
Approval from OJK before the account is opened
A report to PPATK every time the PEP deposits money
Closing the account when the PEP leaves office
quiz.explanation: Article 37 requires a designated senior officer's approval, EDD on source of funds and wealth, and stricter monitoring. There is no OJK pre-approval or automatic reporting of every PEP deposit.

quiz.question: A bank cannot establish the identity of a prospective customer's beneficial owner despite asking. What must it do?
options: Refuse the business relationship or transaction
Open the account and mark it for review next year
Open the account as long as the customer signs a declaration
Apply simplified CDD instead
quiz.explanation: Article 33(12) requires the bank to refuse when it doubts or cannot be sure of the beneficial owner's identity. Simplified CDD is only for assessed low risk.

quiz.question: Siti applies to open a savings account but refuses to provide her source of funds. Under Law 8/2010, what must the bank do?
options: Open the account but block withdrawals
Open the account with a note that information is pending
Refuse or end the relationship and report it to PPATK as a suspicious transaction
Ask OJK for permission to proceed
quiz.explanation: Law 8/2010 requires financial service providers to end the relationship where a customer refuses KYC and to report that action to PPATK as suspicious. POJK 8/2023 also makes refused or closed cases reportable.

quiz.question: During CDD the bank comes to suspect laundering and believes that continuing CDD would alert the customer. What does POJK 8/2023 require?
options: Finish all CDD steps first, then report
Tell the customer the bank needs more time for checks
Close the account immediately without reporting
Stop the CDD process and report the suspicious transaction to PPATK
quiz.explanation: Article 49(3) says that where CDD would breach the anti-tipping-off rule, the bank stops CDD and files an LTKM with PPATK.

quiz.question: Which customers must a bank keep in a separate list under POJK 8/2023?
options: Customers and beneficial owners that meet the bank's high-risk criteria
Every customer with a balance over IDR 500 million
Customers who have closed their accounts
Customers who used non face-to-face onboarding
quiz.explanation: Article 40 requires a separate list of prospective customers, customers, walk-in customers and beneficial owners who meet high-risk criteria. The other groups are not defined that way.

quiz.question: A bank relies on another regulated financial institution's identification and verification of a shared customer. Who is responsible for the CDD?
options: The third party that did the checks
The bank that relies on it
OJK, which supervises both institutions
Responsibility is split evenly between the two
quiz.explanation: Article 46(4) of POJK 8/2023 keeps CDD responsibility with the relying bank, which also needs a written agreement and prompt access to the information and documents.

quiz.question: A low-risk customer on simplified CDD starts receiving transfers that suggest laundering. What happens to the simplified treatment?
options: It continues until the yearly review
It continues because the customer was rated low risk at onboarding
It is suspended only if PPATK asks
It no longer applies, so full CDD and analysis are needed
quiz.explanation: POJK 8/2023 says simplified CDD does not apply where laundering, terrorism financing or proliferation financing is suspected, or specific risk rises.

sessions.title: Reporting to PPATK: LTKM, LTKT, LTKL and Tipping Off
sessions.summary: Spot suspicious transactions, meet PPATK reporting deadlines through goAML, handle postponements and blocking orders, keep records and never tip off.
objectives: Apply the four-limb definition of a suspicious transaction
Meet the deadlines for LTKM, LTKT and LTKL reports
Use postponement, temporary halts and blocking orders correctly
Keep and produce records as the law requires

cards.title: The alert that wouldn't go away
cards.setting: AML/CFT/CPF unit, Jakarta head office. 4:10 pm.

lines.text: Look at this student account from our Yogyakarta branch. Hundreds of small transfers in from strangers every evening, and the money leaves within minutes to e-wallet top-ups.
Declared profile: university student, monthly allowance from parents. That doesn't match hundreds of incoming payments a night.
It looks like a collection account for online gambling deposits. The branch says a man phoned asking why one transfer was 'pending'.
Then we need two answers today: is this an LTKM, and how fast must it reach PPATK?
Welcome to stage three, the Signal Tower. Our job is to turn what we notice into reports PPATK can use, on time and without warning the customer.

cards.title: Four ways a transaction becomes suspicious

scenes.heading: It breaks the pattern
scenes.narration: Under Law 8/2010, a transaction is suspicious if it departs from the customer's profile, characteristics or usual transaction pattern.

scenes.heading: It dodges a report
scenes.narration: It is also suspicious if the customer appears to be structuring it to avoid a report the bank is required to file.

scenes.heading: It may involve proceeds
scenes.narration: A transaction made, or abandoned, using assets suspected to come from crime is suspicious too. Note that attempts count.

scenes.heading: PPATK asks for it
scenes.narration: Finally, PPATK can ask a reporting party to report a transaction because it involves suspected proceeds of crime.

scenes.heading: Then the clock runs
scenes.narration: Once the bank knows of suspicious elements, the report must go to PPATK as soon as possible and no later than three working days.

cards.title: Reports to PPATK and their deadlines
cards.caption: Sources: Law 8/2010, Articles 23, 25 and 26, and PPATK's reporting guidance. All reports go through goAML.

items.label: LTKM: suspicious transaction report
items.detail: At the latest, from when the bank knows of suspicious elements. Applies to ML, TF and PF, including attempts.

items.label: LTKT: cash transaction report
items.detail: Cash of IDR 500 million or more, in one transaction or several in one working day.

items.label: LTKL: cross-border transfer report
items.detail: Fund transfers to and from abroad; PPATK says every such transfer is reported, whatever the amount.

items.label: Report of a postponed transaction
items.detail: When the bank postpones a transaction, it reports to PPATK with the minutes within 24 hours.

cards.question: The AML unit concludes on Monday that the student account's activity is suspicious. Under Law 8/2010, what is the latest the LTKM can reach PPATK?
options: Three working days after the bank knew of the suspicious elements
Fourteen working days after the last transaction
The end of the month, in the monthly batch
Thirty days after the customer was first contacted
cards.explanation: Article 25(1) requires suspicious transaction reports as soon as possible and no later than three working days after the bank knows of the suspicious elements. Fourteen working days applies to cash and cross-border transfer reports.

cards.title: Filing through goAML
cards.body:
PPATK's reporting guidance says that LTKM, LTKT and LTKL reports **must be filed electronically through the goAML application**. Paper or other non-electronic filing is allowed only when:
- communication facilities are not available where the reporting party is based;
- the bank's own facilities suffer a technical failure;
- force majeure prevents electronic filing; or
- PPATK's reporting system is down.

The detailed procedure for financial service providers is set by **PPATK Head Regulation No. 1 of 2021** on filing LTKM, LTKT and LTKL through goAML.

POJK 8/2023 adds that the bank reports suspicious transactions **and attempted transactions** linked to terrorism or proliferation financing, files **correction reports** where needed, and that the AML unit may report directly to PPATK, **even when the transaction involves the bank's own directors or commissioners**.

cards.title: LTKM, LTKT or LTKL?
cards.prompt: Decide which report each situation calls for. Some real cases need more than one report; pick the one the situation describes.

items.text: A routine IDR 600 million cash deposit by a supermarket chain matching its turnover
A customer's USD 2,000 transfer to a relative studying in Australia
A student account receiving hundreds of small payments a night, forwarded to e-wallets
Three cash deposits of IDR 200 million each by the same customer on one working day
An incoming transfer from Hong Kong to an Indonesian importer's account
An applicant walks away when asked for ID after offering to deposit a large sum
A customer splits cash across family accounts after asking what gets reported

items.label: Notice and record
items.detail: Staff note the facts, words and documents at the time.

items.label: Report internally
items.detail: Escalate to the AML unit through a confidential channel.

items.label: Analyse
items.detail: Profile, history, counterparties; ask the customer only with tipping-off in mind.

items.label: Decide and document
items.detail: Suspicion formed or not, with reasons kept on file.

items.label: File the LTKM
items.detail: On goAML, no later than three working days after the bank knows.

items.label: Follow through
items.detail: Review the relationship, keep monitoring and keep the records.

cards.title: The caller at the branch
cards.setting: Bank Lintas Samudra, Yogyakarta branch, customer service desk. Next morning.

lines.text: The man who phoned yesterday now stands at the desk. He says he is the student's uncle and 'helps manage' the account.
(on the phone to the branch) The LTKM went to PPATK through goAML an hour ago. He's asking whether the bank 'reported anything to anyone'.
Anyone could be tempted to calm him down with a white lie, or to tell him the truth. Both are wrong.

cards.title: Did you report me?
cards.situation: The 'uncle' asks the customer service officer, Putri, directly whether the bank has reported the account to PPATK. He is calm but insistent and says he will move the money elsewhere if the bank 'is causing trouble'. What should Putri do?

choices.text: Reassure him that the bank never reports ordinary student accounts
choices.outcome: This is a false statement that engages with the question about reporting and may undermine PPATK's analysis. Staff should not discuss reporting at all, truthfully or otherwise.

choices.text: Tell him honestly that a report was filed, because customers deserve transparency
choices.outcome: This is tipping off. Law 8/2010 forbids directors, commissioners and staff from telling the customer or anyone else about an LTKM being prepared or filed. The penalty reaches 5 years and IDR 1 billion.

choices.text: Say she cannot discuss internal processes, offer the standard service, record the exchange and alert the AML unit at once
choices.outcome: Correct. Putri neither confirms nor denies anything, handles the service request by the book and passes his words and threat to move funds to the AML unit, which may need to update its analysis or file a further report.

choices.text: Refuse to speak to him and call security
choices.outcome: Unnecessary escalation can itself signal that something is wrong. A calm, neutral answer plus prompt internal reporting protects the bank better; security is only for real threats.

cards.title: Protections and powers you should know

cards.front: Does bank secrecy block a report?
cards.back: No. Law 8/2010 says carrying out reporting duties is exempt from the secrecy rules that bind the reporting party.

cards.front: Can staff be sued for reporting?
cards.back: Reporting parties, their officers and staff cannot be prosecuted or sued for reporting under the law, unless they abused their authority.

cards.front: Can the bank pause a transaction?
cards.back: Yes. It may postpone a transaction for up to five working days where proceeds or false documents are suspected.
Yes. PPATK may ask a financial service provider to temporarily halt all or part of a transaction, and the bank must comply.
Investigators, prosecutors or judges may order a block on suspected proceeds; the bank acts immediately and sends minutes within one working day.
Giving information to the supervisory authority, OJK for banks, is not tipping off.

cards.title: Postponing a transaction
cards.prompt: Put the steps Law 8/2010 sets for a bank-initiated postponement in order.
steps: The bank suspects the transaction uses criminal proceeds or a false document
The bank postpones the transaction, for no more than five working days
The postponement is recorded in official minutes (berita acara)
A copy of the minutes is given to the customer
The bank reports the postponement, with the minutes, to PPATK within 24 hours
By the fifth working day the bank decides whether to carry out or refuse the transaction

cards.title: Records and requests
cards.caption: Keep the whole STR trail too: POJK 8/2023 requires records of every step in identifying suspicious transactions.

items.label: Customer identity records
items.detail: After the relationship ends (Law 8/2010), or after a mismatch with the transaction's purpose is found (POJK 8/2023).

items.label: Fund transfer information
items.detail: Information identifying originators and beneficiaries, after the transfer ends (Law 9/2013).

items.label: Producing records on request
items.detail: Maximum time to give OJK or another authority the data and documents it asks for.

items.label: Investigator's block
items.detail: Maximum length of a block ordered under Law 8/2010; it then ends by law.

cards.question: Which disclosure about an LTKM does Law 8/2010 permit?
options: Telling the customer's lawyer, if the customer consents
Confirming the report to a family member managing the account
Mentioning it to the customer to obtain missing documents
Giving information to OJK as the bank's supervisory authority
cards.explanation: Article 12(2) says the tipping-off ban does not apply to information given to the supervisory and regulatory authority. Disclosure to the customer or anyone acting for them is prohibited.

cards.title: Real case: OJK orders banks to block gambling accounts (2023)
Write an LTKM that PPATK can use
cards.body:
- Lead with **why** the activity is suspicious, in plain words.
- Name the limb: off-profile, avoiding a report, suspected proceeds, or PPATK request.
- Give the facts: dates, amounts, counterparties, channels, accounts.
- Explain what the customer said and what CDD shows about the profile.
- Attach supporting analysis and keep your working papers on file.
- Never let the three-working-day deadline slip while you polish the wording.

cards.title: Stage three: what to remember
items: A suspicious transaction is off-profile, designed to avoid reporting, linked to suspected proceeds, or requested by PPATK; attempts count.
LTKM: no later than three working days after the bank knows. LTKT and LTKL: within fourteen working days.
Cash reports start at IDR 500 million in one working day; cross-border transfers are reported whatever the amount.
All reports go through goAML; paper filing is only for listed emergencies.
Reporting overrides secrecy and protects staff acting in good faith; tipping off is a crime.
Keep identity records for at least five years and produce records to OJK within three working days.

cards.prompt: If a customer pushed you hard tomorrow on whether you had reported them, what exact words would you use, and whom would you tell straight afterwards?

quiz.question: Through which application must banks file LTKM, LTKT and LTKL reports with PPATK?
options: SIPENDAR
The OJK reporting portal
BI-FAST
goAML
quiz.explanation: PPATK's reporting guidance requires electronic filing through goAML, with PPATK Head Regulation No. 1 of 2021 setting the procedure for financial service providers. BI-FAST is a payment system.

quiz.question: A customer deposits IDR 300 million in cash in the morning and IDR 250 million in the afternoon of the same working day. Which report is required?
options: None, because each deposit is below IDR 500 million
An LTKL, because the total exceeds IDR 500 million
An LTKT, because cash totalling at least IDR 500 million in one working day is reportable
An LTKT only if the customer is a walk-in customer
quiz.explanation: Law 8/2010 counts one or several cash transactions in one working day toward the IDR 500 million threshold. LTKL is for cross-border transfers.

quiz.question: What is the deadline for filing a cash transaction report (LTKT) with PPATK?
options: Three working days from the transaction
Fourteen working days from the date of the transaction
Twenty-four hours from the transaction
The end of the following month
quiz.explanation: Article 25(2) of Law 8/2010 sets 14 working days for cash transaction reports. Three working days is the deadline for suspicious transaction reports.

quiz.question: A customer's outward transfer of USD 300 to a supplier in Malaysia is routine and fits his profile. What does PPATK's guidance say about reporting it?
options: It is not reportable, because it is below the cash threshold
It is reported as an LTKM, because all foreign transfers are suspicious
It is reported only if it exceeds IDR 100 million
It is reported as an LTKL, because every cross-border transfer is reportable regardless of amount
quiz.explanation: PPATK's guidance says every transfer to or from abroad is reported, whatever the amount, within 14 working days. Being reportable does not make it suspicious.

quiz.question: A bank postpones a transaction because the customer seems to be using a forged document. Within what time must it report the postponement to PPATK?
options: Within three working days, with the LTKM
Within fourteen working days
Only if the customer complains
Within 24 hours, attaching the postponement minutes
quiz.explanation: Article 26 of Law 8/2010 requires a report of the postponement, with the minutes, within 24 hours. The postponement itself may last up to five working days.

quiz.question: An employee fears a customer will sue her for defamation after she escalated a suspicion that led to an LTKM. What does Law 8/2010 say?
options: She is protected only if PPATK later confirms a crime
She is protected only if the report was filed within 24 hours
Reporting parties and their staff cannot be sued or prosecuted for reporting, unless they abused their authority
The bank must indemnify her, but she can still be held liable
quiz.explanation: Article 29 shields reporting parties, officers and staff from civil and criminal action for carrying out reporting duties, except where authority was abused. The protection does not depend on the outcome.

quiz.question: Which situation fits the Law 8/2010 limb about avoiding reports?
options: A customer's salary arrives late from a new employer
A customer splits cash deposits across days to stay below the reporting threshold
A pensioner withdraws cash for a family wedding
A company pays its staff through the bank's payroll service
quiz.explanation: Law 8/2010 treats as suspicious a transaction that seems designed to avoid a report the bank must file. Splitting cash to stay under a threshold is the classic example.

quiz.question: An investigator sends the bank a written order to block a suspect's account. When must the bank carry it out?
options: Within three working days
Immediately after receiving the order
After notifying the customer and allowing an objection
After OJK confirms the order
quiz.explanation: Article 71 of Law 8/2010 requires the reporting party to block immediately on receiving the order, keep the funds in place and deliver minutes within one working day.

quiz.question: OJK asks a bank for CDD records on a customer during an inspection. How quickly must the bank provide them under POJK 8/2023?
options: As soon as possible and no later than three working days
Within fourteen working days
Within thirty days
At the next annual report
quiz.explanation: Article 63(4) requires the bank to provide stored data, information and documents within three working days of a request from OJK or another competent authority.

quiz.question: A customer abandons a large transfer when the teller asks about the source of funds, and the bank suspects the money is criminal proceeds. Can this be reported as an LTKM?
options: No, only completed transactions can be reported
Yes, a transaction abandoned using suspected proceeds can be suspicious
Only if the amount is above IDR 500 million
Only if PPATK has asked about the customer before
quiz.explanation: Law 8/2010 defines a suspicious transaction to include one that is made or cancelled using assets suspected to come from crime. There is no amount threshold for LTKM.

sessions.title: Terrorism and Proliferation Financing: Lists and Immediate Freezing
sessions.summary: Apply Law 9/2013 and POJK 8/2023 to terrorism and proliferation financing: the DTTOT and DPPSPM, immediate freezing, freeze and nil reports, and transfer information.
objectives: Explain the terrorism financing offence and the bank's TF duties
Describe how the DTTOT is created and reaches banks
Freeze and report correctly after a confirmed list match
Handle false positives, joint funds and objections

cards.title: A name on the new list
cards.setting: AML/CFT/CPF unit, Jakarta head office. 7:50 am.

lines.text: OJK's system pushed an updated DTTOT overnight. Our screening found a strong match: a customer at our Denpasar branch. Same full name, same date of birth, same ID number.
Then this is not a 'maybe'. Under POJK 8/2023 a match means an immediate freeze, without delay and without warning the customer.
(from Denpasar) Ketut here. The customer's brother runs a travel agency with him. They hold a joint business account too.
And the brother is already on his way to the branch to withdraw cash for 'urgent payments'.
Stage four, the Frozen Vault. Terrorism and proliferation financing work on a different clock from laundering. Let's learn it.

cards.title: How a name reaches the DTTOT

scenes.heading: The police chief applies
scenes.narration: Under Law 9/2013, the Chief of the Indonesian National Police applies to the Central Jakarta District Court to list a person or corporation as a suspected terrorist or terrorist organisation.

scenes.heading: The court decides
scenes.narration: The application carries the identity, the reasons and supporting documents, plus a foreign ministry recommendation where the material comes from abroad. The court rules within thirty working days.

scenes.heading: The list is issued
scenes.narration: Once the court agrees, the police chief places the name on the DTTOT and must notify the listed person in writing within ten working days.

scenes.heading: It reaches the banks
scenes.narration: The list and every change go to the relevant agencies and supervisors, which pass it on. For banks, OJK delivers the DTTOT and the proliferation list, the DPPSPM, through its own system.

scenes.heading: Funds freeze at once
scenes.narration: Banks must then freeze immediately all funds owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by the listed person, and the freeze lasts as long as the name stays on the list.

items.label: What it lists
items.right: Suspected financiers of weapons of mass destruction

items.label: Freeze report with minutes goes to
items.left: Indonesian National Police, copy to OJK

items.label: If there is no match
items.left: Nil report to the police, copy to OJK
items.right: Nil report to PPATK, copy to OJK

items.label: Deadline for freeze or nil report
items.left: 3 working days from receiving the list
items.right: 3 working days from receiving the list

items.label: Suspicious transaction report
items.left: LTKM to PPATK on any match
items.right: LTKM to PPATK on any match

cards.question: Rizal confirms the Denpasar customer matches the DTTOT. Where does the freeze report with its minutes go?
options: To PPATK only
To the Central Jakarta District Court
To the Indonesian National Police, with a copy to OJK
To Bank Indonesia, with a copy to PPATK
cards.explanation: POJK 8/2023 sends the DTTOT freeze report and minutes to the National Police with a copy to OJK, within three working days of receiving the list. For the DPPSPM the report goes to PPATK. A match is also reported to PPATK as an LTKM.

cards.title: The terrorism financing offence and its duties
cards.body:
**Law 9/2013** makes it a crime to deliberately **provide, collect, give or lend funds**, directly or indirectly, intending them to be used, wholly or partly, for a terrorist act, a terrorist organisation or a terrorist. The maximum is **15 years** in prison and a fine of **IDR 1 billion**. Conspiracy, attempt and assistance carry the same penalty; planning or organising the offence can mean **life imprisonment** or up to **20 years**. Corporations face fines of up to **IDR 100 billion**.

Duties for banks:
- **Report** TF-related suspicious transactions to PPATK no later than **three working days** after knowing of them. A deliberate failure can bring an administrative fine of up to **IDR 1 billion**, imposed by the supervisor.
- **No tipping off:** up to **5 years** and **IDR 1 billion**.
- **Know your customer** under the supervisor's rules, including for TF risks.
- **Freeze** listed persons' funds immediately.

cards.title: A confirmed list match: what happens next
cards.prompt: Put the bank's steps after screening finds a match in the order POJK 8/2023 requires.
steps: Confirm that the customer's identity and other information match the list entry
Freeze immediately all funds the person owns or controls, without delay and without telling them first
Prepare the official freeze minutes (berita acara)
Send the freeze report and minutes to the police for the DTTOT, or PPATK for the DPPSPM, copying OJK, within three working days
Report the match to PPATK as a suspicious transaction (LTKM)
Keep the freeze in place for as long as the name stays on the list

cards.title: Freeze, escalate or clear?
cards.prompt: Screening has produced these alerts against the DTTOT. Decide the right handling for each.

items.text: Full name, date of birth and national ID number all match the list entry
Same common name, but different date of birth, nationality and ID number
Name matches an alias on the list, date of birth matches, no ID number held by the bank
A beneficial owner of a corporate customer matches the list on name, date of birth and passport
Partial name match with a listed organisation; the customer is a registered charity with a similar name
Name matches, but the customer was born 40 years after the listed person

cards.title: The brother at the counter
cards.setting: Bank Lintas Samudra, Denpasar branch. 9:30 am.

lines.text: The brother is here. He says half the money in the joint travel agency account is his, and he needs IDR 200 million today to pay hotels.
The freeze covers funds owned or controlled directly or indirectly, wholly or jointly with others. The joint account is in scope.
He's not on the list himself. Isn't freezing his share unfair?
There's a lawful route for that: objections go to the police chief, and a court can follow. The branch doesn't decide it at the counter.

cards.title: Releasing 'his half'
cards.situation: The listed customer's brother is not on the DTTOT. He shows documents suggesting he contributed half the funds in their joint business account, which the bank froze this morning. He asks Ketut to release IDR 200 million so the agency can pay suppliers, and says the bank will be 'responsible for ruining the business'. What should Ketut do?

choices.text: Release IDR 200 million, since the brother is not listed and has evidence of his share
choices.outcome: This breaks the freeze. POJK 8/2023 extends the freeze to funds the listed person owns or controls jointly with others, and the bank must not make funds available to listed persons. Only the lawful objection route can lift it.

choices.text: Keep the freeze, tell him neutrally that the funds cannot be released, and refer the matter to the AML unit and legal team
choices.outcome: Correct. Ketut keeps the funds frozen, avoids discussing the list or reports, and escalates. The AML unit can explain to the brother, through the proper channel, that objections go to the police chief under Law 9/2013, and logs his request as possible sanction evasion.

choices.text: Close the joint account and send the brother a cheque for his half
choices.outcome: Closing the account and paying out moves frozen funds. The freeze must stay in place while the listed person remains on the DTTOT.

choices.text: Keep the freeze but tell him the account is blocked because his brother is a terror suspect
choices.outcome: Keeping the freeze is right, but volunteering the reason risks disclosing information beyond what the process allows and could alert others. Let the AML unit manage communications through the proper channel.

cards.back: Immediate freezing, without delay and without telling the customer beforehand, as soon as a list match is confirmed.
Official minutes recording what was frozen, when and by whom; they go with the freeze report.
Nil report: if screening finds no match, the bank still reports that to the police (DTTOT) or PPATK (DPPSPM), copying OJK.
Banned: the bank must not provide, give or lend funds to or for listed persons or corporations.
POJK 8/2023 requires banks to identify, assess, understand and mitigate the risk that customers try to get around the lists.
A listed person can object to a freeze in writing to the police chief; if refused, the dispute can go to the Central Jakarta District Court.

cards.title: The CFT and CPF clocks
cards.caption: Freezing is not a judgement on the customer's guilt; it is a legal duty that follows the list.

items.label: Freeze after a confirmed match
items.detail: Without delay and without prior notice to the customer or beneficial owner.

items.label: Freeze or nil report
items.detail: From the day the bank receives the DTTOT or DPPSPM through OJK's system.

items.label: TF suspicious transaction report
items.detail: From when the bank knows of the TF-related suspicious transaction (Law 9/2013).

items.label: Court ruling on a listing
items.detail: Central Jakarta District Court decides the police chief's application.

cards.title: Which rule says so?
cards.prompt: Match each duty to the instrument that sets it.

pairs.left: Refuse a transfer if the sender won't give originator details
pairs.right: Law 9/2013: transfer senders must supply full information or the transfer is refused

pairs.left: Keep transfer data on senders and recipients
pairs.right: Law 9/2013: the sending provider keeps it for at least five years

pairs.left: Check a foreign respondent bank first
pairs.right: POJK 8/2023: understand its business, reputation and home AML/CFT/CPF regime before cross-border correspondent banking

pairs.left: Keep the lists up to date
pairs.right: POJK 8/2023: maintain the DTTOT and DPPSPM delivered through OJK's system

pairs.left: Report a deliberate TF reporting failure
pairs.right: Law 9/2013: the supervisor may impose an administrative fine of up to IDR 1 billion

cards.question: Which funds does the immediate freeze under POJK 8/2023 cover?
options: Only accounts held solely in the listed person's name
Funds owned or controlled by the listed person, directly or indirectly, wholly or jointly with others
Only funds deposited after the person was listed
Only funds above IDR 100 million
cards.explanation: Article 53(5) extends the freeze to funds owned or controlled directly or indirectly, however obtained, held wholly or jointly with other parties. There is no threshold or date limit.

cards.title: Inside the DTTOT: what PPATK publishes
Screening hygiene that examiners check
cards.body:
- Load every list update from OJK's system the day it arrives and keep evidence of when.
- Screen customers, walk-in customers **and beneficial owners**, not just account names.
- Use aliases, dates of birth and ID numbers to resolve matches; record why each alert was cleared.
- Re-screen the whole customer base after each update, not only new customers.
- Send freeze or nil reports within three working days, every time.

cards.title: Stage four: what to remember
items: Law 9/2013 punishes providing or collecting funds for terrorism with up to 15 years and IDR 1 billion; organisers can face life.
TF-related suspicious transactions go to PPATK within three working days; deliberate failure risks an administrative fine of up to IDR 1 billion.
OJK delivers the DTTOT and DPPSPM to banks; on a confirmed match, freeze immediately, without delay and without warning.
Freeze reports and nil reports are due within three working days: DTTOT to the police, DPPSPM to PPATK, both copied to OJK.
Freezes cover funds owned or controlled directly, indirectly or jointly, and last while the name stays listed.
Objections go to the police chief and then the court, never to the branch counter.

cards.prompt: Where in your daily work could you be the person who notices a listed name or someone trying to work around a freeze? What would you do in the first ten minutes?

quiz.question: What is the maximum prison term for providing funds to a terrorist organisation under Article 4 of Law 9/2013?
options: 15 years
5 years
20 years
10 years
quiz.explanation: Article 4 sets up to 15 years and a fine of up to IDR 1 billion. Planning or organising the offence under Article 6 can mean life or up to 20 years.

quiz.question: Who applies to have a person placed on the DTTOT?
options: PPATK, to OJK
OJK, to the Supreme Court
The bank that finds suspicious transactions, to the police
The Chief of the Indonesian National Police, to the Central Jakarta District Court
quiz.explanation: Article 27 of Law 9/2013 gives the police chief the role of applying to the Central Jakarta District Court, which rules on the listing.

quiz.question: Screening confirms that a customer matches the DPPSPM. Where does the freeze report and minutes go?
options: To PPATK, with a copy to OJK
To the National Police, with a copy to OJK
To the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
To OJK only
quiz.explanation: For the proliferation financing list POJK 8/2023 sends freeze and nil reports to PPATK, copying OJK. DTTOT reports go to the National Police.

quiz.question: A bank receives an updated DTTOT and finds no customer matches. What must it do?
options: Nothing, since no freeze was needed
Send a nil report to PPATK within fourteen working days
Send a nil report to the police, with a copy to OJK, within three working days
Inform the customers who were screened
quiz.explanation: POJK 8/2023 requires a nil report to the National Police, copied to OJK, within three working days of receiving the DTTOT. For the DPPSPM the nil report goes to PPATK.

quiz.question: When must a bank freeze funds after confirming a DTTOT match?
options: Within three working days, after writing to the customer
After the police send a separate court order to the bank
After OJK approves the freeze
Immediately, without delay and without notifying the customer first
quiz.explanation: Article 53(4) requires immediate freezing without delay and without prior notice. The three-working-day period applies to the freeze report, not to the freeze itself.

quiz.question: A listed person believes the freeze of his account is wrong. Under Law 9/2013, to whom does he first send a written objection?
options: The bank's branch manager
The Chief of the Indonesian National Police
OJK's banking supervisors
PPATK's head
quiz.explanation: Article 29 of Law 9/2013 sends objections to the police chief. If the objection is refused, the person can bring a civil claim in the Central Jakarta District Court.

quiz.question: A bank deliberately fails to report a TF-related suspicious transaction to PPATK. What administrative sanction does Law 9/2013 set?
options: A fine of up to IDR 100 billion imposed by PPATK
Automatic revocation of the bank's licence
A fine of up to IDR 1 billion imposed by the supervisory authority
A written warning only
quiz.explanation: Article 13 of Law 9/2013 allows an administrative fine of up to IDR 1 billion, imposed by the supervisory and regulatory authority, for deliberate failure to report within three working days.

quiz.question: How long does a freeze on a DTTOT-listed person's funds last?
options: Thirty working days, then it ends by law
For as long as the person remains on the list
Five working days, like a postponement
Until the bank's next annual review
quiz.explanation: Article 28(5) of Law 9/2013 keeps the freeze in place while the identity stays on the DTTOT. The 30-day limit belongs to other blocking powers.

quiz.question: A customer asks to send money abroad but refuses to give the originator's address and source of funds. What does Law 9/2013 require?
options: The bank must refuse the transfer
The bank may send it and report later
The bank sends it but files an LTKL marked incomplete
The bank must close the customer's account at once
quiz.explanation: Article 18 of Law 9/2013 requires the financial service provider to refuse a transfer when the customer does not give the required information.

quiz.question: Under POJK 8/2023, which customers must be screened against the DTTOT and DPPSPM?
options: Only new customers onboarded after the list update
Customers and also their beneficial owners
Only customers who send cross-border transfers
Only corporate customers
quiz.explanation: POJK 8/2023 requires matching customers' identities against the lists and freezing where the customer or beneficial owner matches. Existing customers are screened when a list update arrives.

sessions.title: The Bank's Programme: Board, People, Training and Sanctions
sessions.summary: See the programme as OJK's examiners do: five pillars, board and AML unit roles, risk assessment and policy cycles, staff screening, yearly training and OJK sanctions.
objectives: Describe the five pillars of POJK 8/2023
Explain the duties of directors, commissioners and the AML unit
Plan training and staff screening that meet POJK 8/2023
Describe OJK's administrative sanctions and fines

cards.title: Six weeks before the examiners
cards.setting: Board meeting room, Bank Lintas Samudra head office, Jakarta. 3:00 pm.

lines.text: OJK's examiners arrive in six weeks. Ketut, where are we on AML/CFT/CPF training?
Eighty-two percent of staff completed this year's module. The gap is mostly new joiners in the branches and the payments operations team.
Those are exactly the people POJK 8/2023 names: staff in relevant units and new employees. And we have no evaluation of whether the training worked.
Also, our individual risk assessment update is due to OJK by the end of June, and the policy review flagged changes we haven't written yet.
So the question isn't whether we have a programme on paper. It's whether every pillar works.
Final stage: the Council Chamber. Let's look at the programme the way OJK's examiners will.

scenes.heading: Active board oversight
scenes.narration: Pillar one: the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners actively oversee the programme. Directors propose and run it; commissioners approve and supervise.

scenes.heading: Policies and procedures
scenes.narration: Pillar two: written policies and procedures, built on the risk assessment, covering CDD, beneficial owners, refusals, monitoring, records and reporting to PPATK.

scenes.heading: Internal control
scenes.narration: Pillar three: an effective and independent internal control system, with clear limits of authority and independent checks that the programme works.

scenes.heading: Management information system
scenes.narration: Pillar four: systems that identify, analyse, monitor and report customers' transaction patterns, built on a single customer identification file.

scenes.heading: People and training
scenes.narration: Pillar five: human resources and training, meaning screening of new staff, knowing your employees, and AML, CFT and CPF training at least once a year.

cards.title: The programme's yearly rhythm
cards.caption: POJK 8/2023 allows several of these steps more than once a year when risk, size or major changes require it.

items.label: Assess risk
items.detail: Update the individual ML/TF/PF risk assessment at least yearly; send it to OJK by the end of June.

items.label: Review policies
items.detail: Review written policies at least yearly; draft any changes within six months of the review.

items.label: Train people
items.detail: Train officers and staff at least once a year, more often where risk or big changes call for it.

items.label: Monitor and report
items.detail: Run monitoring, list screening and reporting to PPATK every day.

items.label: Test independently
items.detail: Independent checks confirm the programme actually works; fix what they find.

cards.title: Who does what?
cards.prompt: Match each role to its duty under POJK 8/2023.

pairs.right: Proposes policies, sets up the AML unit and ensures yearly training, especially for relevant units and new joiners
Approves and evaluates the policies and oversees how the directors carry out their duties
Analyses risk yearly, monitors customers, compiles reports to PPATK and recommends training needs
For banks, the AML unit or officer sits under this member of the Board of Directors
Test whether the programme is effective, as part of internal control
Screens new hires and monitors employee profiles under know your employee

cards.question: How often must a bank train its officers and staff on AML, CFT and CPF under POJK 8/2023?
options: Once on joining and then every three years
Only when OJK issues a new regulation
Every two years for all staff
At least once a year, and more often if risk or major changes require it
cards.explanation: Article 72 requires continuous, periodic training at least once a year, with extra sessions where the bank's risk assessment, size, complexity or major events call for it. Article 8 makes directors ensure relevant units and new employees attend.

cards.title: The people pillar: screening, KYE and training
Does this training plan meet POJK 8/2023?
cards.prompt: Sort each element of Bank Lintas Samudra's draft plan.

items.text: Every officer and employee gets AML/CFT/CPF training at least once a year
New joiners wait for the next annual cycle, up to eleven months away
The module covers Law 8/2010, Law 9/2013, POJK 8/2023, typologies and each role
Completion is tracked, but nobody evaluates whether the training worked
Payments operations get an extra session after a new instant-transfer product launches
The module covers money laundering only, with nothing on proliferation financing
Some sessions are run jointly with PPATK and the banking association

cards.title: What does a failure cost?
cards.setting: Director's office, head office. The next day.

lines.text: Suppose OJK finds our training and risk assessment fall short. What exactly can it do to us?
POJK 8/2023 lists the sanctions, from a written warning with an order to act, up to a ban on individuals acting as a bank's main party.
