And late reports have their own daily fine. The risk assessment update to OJK is one of those reports.
Then let's see the numbers, and let's decide how to close the gaps before the examiners do it for us.

cards.title: OJK's administrative fines under POJK 8/2023
cards.caption: Fines do not end the duty: the bank must still comply and still submit the missing report.

items.label: Fine cap for a bank
items.detail: Of the previous year's net profit, up to IDR 100 billion a year, for breaches of the programme duties.

items.label: Fine cap for an individual
items.detail: Maximum for a person under the same fine provisions.

items.label: Late report, commercial bank
items.detail: Per working day late, per report, up to IDR 3 million per report.

items.label: Report not submitted
items.detail: For commercial banks: a report more than 30 working days late counts as not submitted.

cards.title: The training budget squeeze
cards.situation: Finance asks to cut this year's AML/CFT/CPF training budget. Their proposal: skip this year's refresher for everyone, roll it into a 'bigger' programme next year, and give new joiners a reading pack instead of training. Agus asks you for a recommendation before the board meeting. What do you advise?

choices.text: Accept the proposal: a bigger programme next year covers two years at once
choices.outcome: Skipping a year breaches the at-least-yearly duty in POJK 8/2023, and the directors are responsible for making sure staff, especially new joiners, attend. A double session next year does not cure the gap.

choices.text: Keep yearly training for all, prioritise relevant units and new joiners, use cheaper formats such as e-learning and PPATK sessions, and add an evaluation
choices.outcome: Correct. The rule fixes the minimum frequency and content, not the delivery method. A risk-based plan that keeps every employee trained yearly, focuses on the units the regulation names and evaluates results meets the rule at lower cost.

choices.text: Train only branch staff this year and exempt head office
choices.outcome: Partly right on prioritising the front line, but POJK 8/2023 covers officers and staff generally, and head office units such as payments and treasury are often the most relevant ones.

choices.text: Replace training with a signed declaration that staff have read the AML policy
choices.outcome: A declaration is not training and does not cover typologies, laws or roles. It would also fail the duty to evaluate training.

cards.back: A warning or written reprimand, together with an order to take specific action.
Capped at 1% of the previous year's net profit and IDR 100 billion a year for a bank; deferred for a bank that made a loss.
OJK can restrict certain business activities of the bank.
OJK can lower the assessment of factors that make up the bank's soundness rating.
OJK can freeze certain business activities.
An individual can be banned from acting as a main party of a financial institution.
OJK may announce sanctions to the public, and a sanction never removes the duty to comply.

cards.title: What changed with POJK 8/2023
cards.caption: Older OJK circulars, such as the 2017 freezing guidance, still apply where they are consistent with POJK 8/2023.

items.label: Scope
items.right: Adds proliferation financing of weapons of mass destruction

items.label: Lists
items.right: Both the DTTOT and the proliferation list (DPPSPM)

items.label: Training
items.right: At least once a year, with evaluation

cards.question: Which staff must pass pre-employment screening under POJK 8/2023?
options: Only staff in the AML unit and branches
Only permanent staff above supervisor grade
Permanent and non-permanent staff from the lowest grade up to one level below the boards
Only members of the Board of Directors
cards.explanation: Article 71 requires screening for permanent and non-permanent staff, including senior officers and experts, from the lowest level up to one level below the directors and commissioners. Know-your-employee monitoring then runs up to the boards themselves.

cards.title: Inspection findings at Bank Lintas Samudra (the quest's story)
cards.body:
*This is the quest's own fictional story.* Six weeks later, OJK's examiners close their visit with four findings:

1. **Training:** 14% of new joiners had no AML/CFT/CPF training within the year, and no evaluation existed. The directors must fix this, since POJK 8/2023 makes them responsible for attendance.
2. **Risk assessment:** the individual assessment did not refer to Indonesia's national and sectoral risk assessments, which the regulation requires.
3. **Screening:** beneficial owners of corporate customers were not screened against the DPPSPM.
4. **Policies:** changes flagged in last year's policy review were drafted after more than six months.

The examiners order corrective actions with deadlines and warn that fines are possible. Agus presents the action plan to both boards, and the AML unit tracks every item to closure.

cards.title: Build the evidence file before anyone asks
Stage five: what to remember
items: The programme stands on five pillars: board oversight, policies and procedures, internal control, MIS, and people and training.
Update the risk assessment yearly and send it to OJK by the end of June; review policies yearly.
Directors ensure officers and staff, especially relevant units and new joiners, are trained at least once a year; training is evaluated.
Screen new hires up to one level below the boards and apply know-your-employee monitoring up to the boards.
OJK can warn, fine (up to 1% of prior-year profit, capped at IDR 100 billion a year), restrict, downgrade, freeze activities or ban individuals.

cards.prompt: If OJK's examiners asked you tomorrow to prove your own part of the programme works, what evidence could you show them, and what is missing?

quiz.question: Which of these is one of the five pillars of the programme under POJK 8/2023?
options: Marketing and sales targets
Human resources and training
Customer satisfaction surveys
Branch expansion planning
quiz.explanation: Article 3 lists active board oversight, policies and procedures, internal control, management information systems, and human resources and training.

quiz.question: By when must a bank send OJK its updated individual ML/TF/PF risk assessment each year?
options: By the end of March
By the end of December
Within fourteen working days of the year end
By the end of June
quiz.explanation: Article 74 of POJK 8/2023 requires the yearly update of the risk assessment to reach OJK by the end of June at the latest.

quiz.question: Under POJK 8/2023, who approves the bank's AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures?
options: The head of the AML unit alone
OJK, before they take effect
The Board of Commissioners, on the directors' proposal
PPATK, during its compliance audit
quiz.explanation: Directors propose the written policies and procedures; the Board of Commissioners approves and evaluates them (Articles 8 and 9).

quiz.question: In a commercial bank, to whom does the special AML/CFT/CPF unit or officer report?
options: The head of internal audit
The Board of Commissioners directly
The member of the Board of Directors who oversees compliance
The head of the largest branch
quiz.explanation: Article 11 places the unit or officer in the organisation structure, responsible to the directors, and for banks under the director in charge of the compliance function.

quiz.question: A bank's yearly policy review identifies needed changes. By when must the changes be drafted?
options: Within six months of the review result
Within three working days
Before the next review a year later
Within thirty working days
quiz.explanation: Article 17(5) of POJK 8/2023 requires changes to be drawn up no later than six months after the review result.

quiz.question: What is the maximum yearly fine OJK can impose on a commercial bank under the general fine provisions of POJK 8/2023?
options: IDR 5 billion regardless of profit
0.5% of total assets, with no cap
IDR 1 billion per breach
1% of the previous year's net profit, capped at IDR 100 billion
quiz.explanation: Article 79 caps fines at 1% of prior-year net profit and IDR 100 billion a year for institutions, and IDR 5 billion a year for individuals.

quiz.question: Which of the following is included in the minimum content of AML/CFT/CPF training under POJK 8/2023?
options: Sales techniques for high-value products
Typologies of ML, TF and PF, and each employee's role
The bank's dividend policy
Personal tax planning for staff
quiz.explanation: Article 72(3) covers the laws and regulations, techniques, methods and typologies, and the bank's policies and procedures with employees' roles and responsibilities.

quiz.question: A commercial bank sends a required report to OJK ten working days late. What fine does POJK 8/2023 set?
options: IDR 10 million, because any late report counts as not submitted
IDR 100,000 per working day late, up to IDR 3 million for that report
IDR 1 billion, as for a TF reporting failure
No fine, only a written warning
quiz.explanation: Article 78 sets IDR 100,000 per working day per report, up to IDR 3 million per report, for commercial banks. A report counts as not submitted only after 30 working days late.

quiz.question: A bank's know-your-employee monitoring under POJK 8/2023 must cover which staff?
options: Only staff handling cash
Staff from the lowest level up to and including the directors and commissioners
Only staff below managerial grade
Only staff in the AML unit
quiz.explanation: Article 71(b) applies know-your-employee monitoring from the lowest level up to the Board of Directors and Board of Commissioners. Pre-employment screening stops one level below the boards.

quiz.question: Bank Lintas Samudra has a subsidiary abroad in a country whose AML rules are looser than POJK 8/2023. Which standard must the subsidiary apply?
options: The POJK 8/2023 standard
The host country's looser rules
Whichever rules the subsidiary's board prefers
Only FATF's general recommendations
quiz.explanation: Article 67 requires offices and subsidiaries abroad to apply POJK 8/2023 where host-country standards are looser; where the host country is stricter, they follow the host rules.

regulators: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
Indonesian National Police (DTTOT listing and freezing reports)

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Five-pillar programme, risk assessment, board and AML unit duties, CDD, beneficial owners, PEPs, EDD, list screening and immediate freezing, records, staff screening, training at least yearly, reporting and administrative sanctions.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2010 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pencucian Uang (Law 8/2010 on the Prevention and Eradication of Money Laundering)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Laundering offences and penalties, tipping off, KYC, five-year records, suspicious reports within three working days, cash and cross-border reports within fourteen working days, postponement, protection of reporters and blocking orders.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 9 Tahun 2013 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pendanaan Terorisme (Law 9/2013 on the Prevention and Eradication of Terrorism Financing)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Terrorism financing offence and penalties, tipping off, TF suspicious reports within three working days, transfer information, DTTOT listing, immediate freezing and objections.

references.title: SEOJK Nomor 38/SEOJK.01/2017 tentang Pedoman Pemblokiran Secara Serta Merta atas Dana Nasabah di Sektor Jasa Keuangan yang Identitasnya Tercantum dalam DTTOT (OJK Circular 38/2017: immediate freezing)
references.note: Step-by-step guidance for freezing, without delay, the funds of customers named on the DTTOT and reporting the freeze; kept alive by POJK 8/2023 where consistent with it.

references.title: Pedoman Pelaporan (PPATK reporting guidance for reporting parties)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: Report types (LTKM, LTKT, LTKL), cross-border transfers reportable whatever the amount, mandatory electronic filing through goAML with limited exceptions, and PPATK Head Regulation 1/2021 for financial service providers.

references.title: Daftar Terduga Teroris dan Organisasi Teroris (DTTOT) (Domestic list of suspected terrorists and terrorist organisations)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: Targeted financial sanctions under Law 9/2013: court-based listing, immediate freezing, objections, delisting, basic-necessities exception and the 2015 joint regulation.

references.title: Keanggotaan Penuh FATF: Bekal Penting Menuju Indonesia Emas 2045 (PPATK press release on full FATF membership)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: Indonesia accepted as the FATF's 40th member on 25 October 2023 after observer status from 29 June 2018 and completion of all 48 action-plan items.

references.title: Siaran Pers SP 190/OJK/GKPB/XII/2023: OJK Minta Perbankan Blokir Rekening Aktifitas Kejahatan dan Judi Online (OJK press release on blocking accounts used for crime and online gambling)
references.note: OJK ordered banks to block more than 4,000 online gambling accounts in three months and asked for stronger CDD/EDD, profiling systems and LTKM reporting.

references.title: PPATK Hentikan Sementara Transaksi Rekening Dormant untuk Lindungi Kepentingan Publik (PPATK press release on halting dormant accounts)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: More than 28,000 traded accounts were used for online gambling deposits in 2024; PPATK temporarily halted dormant accounts under Law 8/2010.

bank.question: A notary's client converts the proceeds of a large tax crime into foreign currency and property in his children's names to hide where the money came from. Under Law 8/2010, what is the maximum fine he faces for the Article 3 offence?
options: IDR 1 billion
IDR 5 billion
IDR 10 billion
IDR 100 billion
bank.explanation: Article 3 (placing, converting, transferring to hide origin) carries up to 20 years and IDR 10 billion. IDR 5 billion is the Article 4 cap and IDR 100 billion the corporate cap.

bank.question: Which statement about predicate crimes under Law 8/2010 is correct?
options: Only corruption, narcotics and terrorism are predicate crimes
Tax crimes are excluded because they are handled by the tax office
Crimes committed abroad never count as predicate crimes
Besides the listed crimes, any crime punishable by four years or more can generate proceeds
bank.explanation: Article 2 lists many crimes, including tax, banking, fraud and forestry crimes, and adds any crime carrying four years or more, at home or abroad if also criminal in Indonesia.

bank.question: PT Graha Lestari's president director orders staff to route bribery proceeds through company accounts for the company's benefit. Who may be punished under Law 8/2010?
options: Only the junior staff who made the transfers
Only the company, as directors act on its behalf
No one, because companies cannot launder money
The company and/or its controlling personnel, such as the president director
bank.explanation: Articles 6 and 7 allow penalties against the corporation and/or its controlling personnel when the act was ordered by them, served the company's purpose and was meant to benefit it.

bank.question: Which authority imposes administrative sanctions on a bank for failing to file reports to PPATK under Law 8/2010?
options: The supervisory and regulatory authority, which for banks is OJK
PPATK in every case
The Central Jakarta District Court
The Ministry of Finance
bank.explanation: Article 30 gives the supervisory and regulatory authority the power to impose these sanctions; PPATK steps in only where no such authority exists. OJK is that authority for banks.

bank.question: OJK finds during an inspection that a bank failed to report a suspicious transaction. What does Law 8/2010 require OJK to do with this finding?
options: Pass the finding to PPATK promptly
File the LTKM itself on the bank's behalf
Keep the finding confidential within OJK
Wait for the bank to report it within fourteen days
bank.explanation: Article 32 requires the supervisory and regulatory authority to send unreported suspicious transactions it discovers to PPATK promptly.

bank.question: A relationship manager deliberately tells a corporate client's finance director that the bank is drafting an LTKM about the client. Who else, besides staff, does the tipping-off ban in Law 8/2010 cover?
options: Only staff of PPATK
Only external auditors
Directors, commissioners and managers of the reporting party
No one else; it applies only to front-line staff
bank.explanation: Article 12 covers directors, commissioners, managers and employees of reporting parties, and separately PPATK and supervisory staff.

bank.question: What did PPATK report about Indonesia's admission to the FATF in October 2023?
options: Indonesia was admitted as an observer for the first time
Indonesia was placed on the FATF list of high-risk jurisdictions
Indonesia became the 40th member after completing all items in its action plan
Indonesia joined after the FATF waived its mutual evaluation
bank.explanation: PPATK's release says Indonesia was accepted by acclamation as the 40th member on 25 October 2023, after being an observer since 2018 and completing all 48 action-plan items.

bank.question: Article 5 of Law 8/2010 penalises receiving or controlling criminal proceeds. Which combination of maximum penalties applies?
options: 20 years in prison and an IDR 5 billion fine
15 years in prison and an IDR 1 billion fine
5 years in prison and an IDR 1 billion fine
4 years in prison and no fine
bank.explanation: Article 5 sets up to 5 years and IDR 1 billion. 20 years and IDR 5 billion is Article 4; 15 years and IDR 1 billion is the TF offence under Law 9/2013.

bank.question: A prospective customer opens an account through the bank's app. The bank checks her identity against national population data and asks only for a password and PIN. Is this enough under POJK 8/2023?
options: Yes; any two factors satisfy the rule
Yes; population data alone is sufficient
No; app onboarding is not allowed for banks
No; it needs at least something she is and something she has
bank.explanation: Article 21 requires non face-to-face electronic verification to use population data and at least two factors: something you are and something you have. A password and PIN are both 'something you know'.

bank.question: A trust opens an account at the bank. Whose identities must the bank identify and verify as beneficial owners under POJK 8/2023?
options: Only the trustee who signs the account documents
The settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiaries and anyone controlling the trust
Only the beneficiaries who receive payments
Only the settlor who created the trust
bank.explanation: Article 33(4) lists the settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiaries or class of beneficiaries, and any individual who controls the trust.

bank.question: A state-owned enterprise with majority government ownership opens an account. Its ownership information is publicly available and reliable. What does POJK 8/2023 allow?
options: Beneficial owner checks do not apply to state-owned enterprises at all
The bank must always collect a full beneficial owner declaration from the customer
The bank must ask OJK to verify the owner
The bank need not ask the customer again for beneficial owner identity data it can rely on publicly
bank.explanation: Article 34 still applies beneficial owner verification to state bodies, majority state-owned companies and listed companies, but lets the bank rely on adequate and reliable public information; if in doubt it must ask the customer.

bank.question: Which factor is NOT among those POJK 8/2023 lists for grouping customers by risk level?
options: The customer's ownership structure, for companies
The products, services and delivery channels used
The frequency of transactions
The customer's religion
bank.explanation: Article 20 lists identity, business location, profile, frequency of transactions, business activity, ownership structure, products, services and channels, and other relevant information. Religion is not a risk factor.

bank.question: The bank's customer is a former senior official of an international organisation, who served as a deputy director. How does POJK 8/2023 classify her?
options: As an ordinary customer, because international organisations are outside Indonesia
As a domestic PEP only if she is Indonesian
As a PEP only if she still holds the post today
As a PEP, because she held a prominent function in an international organisation
bank.explanation: Article 2(2) treats people with prominent functions in international organisations, such as directors, deputy directors and board members, as one of the three PEP groups.

bank.question: A long-standing customer's account suddenly receives large transfers that do not fit his profile. The bank asks him to explain, and his answer is vague and unconvincing. What does POJK 8/2023 require?
options: Close the account immediately without reporting
Report the transactions to PPATK as suspicious
Wait for six months of further activity
Ask OJK whether to report
bank.explanation: Article 52 requires analysis of off-profile transactions; the bank may ask the customer, minding tipping off, and must report an LTKM if the explanation is not convincing.

bank.question: A bank refuses to open an account because the applicant's documents appear forged. What else must it do under POJK 8/2023?
options: Return the documents and take no further action
Report the applicant to OJK only
Complete identification as far as possible, document the case and report it to PPATK
Open a restricted account so the applicant can be monitored
bank.explanation: Article 49 requires refusal, but the bank still completes identification and verification where possible, documents the case and reports it to PPATK as a suspicious transaction.

bank.question: Customers from a country the FATF has publicly identified as high risk, with a call for countermeasures, ask to open accounts. What must the bank apply under POJK 8/2023?
options: Simplified CDD, since the FATF already monitors the country
A blanket ban on all customers with any link to the country
Standard CDD, as POJK 8/2023 does not mention FATF lists
EDD and countermeasures proportionate to the risk, in line with the FATF publication
bank.explanation: Article 41 requires EDD and proportionate countermeasures for relationships with high-risk countries named by the FATF, adjusted to the FATF publication, and independent countermeasures where the FATF lists a country without a call.

bank.question: What must the directors approve in connection with updating customer data under POJK 8/2023?
options: The data-updating plan report and the report on its realisation
Every individual change to a customer's address
Each customer's annual risk score
The list of dormant accounts closed each month
bank.explanation: Article 51 requires the bank to prepare a data-updating plan and a realisation report, both approved by the Board of Directors.

bank.question: On Tuesday a teller notices odd activity but does not escalate it until the following Monday, when the AML unit confirms suspicion. Why is this a problem under Law 8/2010?
options: The three-working-day deadline runs from when the bank knows of suspicious elements, so internal delay eats into it
There is no problem, since the deadline starts when PPATK is told
The deadline is fourteen working days, so a week's delay is fine
The deadline only starts after the customer is interviewed
bank.explanation: Article 25(1) runs the LTKM deadline from when the financial service provider knows of the suspicious elements. Knowledge held by staff can count for the bank, so slow internal escalation creates risk.

bank.question: Which cash transactions are exempt from the LTKT duty under Law 8/2010?
options: All cash deposits by companies with an account over five years old
Transactions with the government and the central bank, and salary or pension payments
Any cash transaction below IDR 1 billion
Cash deposits by PEPs approved by a senior officer
bank.explanation: Article 23(4) exempts transactions with the government and central bank, salary or pension payments, and other transactions PPATK sets or approves. The bank must keep a list of exempted transactions.

bank.question: PPATK asks a bank to temporarily halt transactions on an account. What must the bank do?
options: Comply only after notifying the customer and waiting for objections
Comply and record the halt in official minutes
Refuse unless a court order is attached
Comply only if OJK confirms the request
bank.explanation: Law 8/2010 lets PPATK request a temporary halt and POJK 8/2023 makes compliance mandatory for the bank; the halt is recorded in minutes.

bank.question: The bank's Head of Treasury, a director, makes unusual transfers through his own account that look like laundering. What does POJK 8/2023 allow the AML unit to do?
options: Report the transactions directly to PPATK, even though they involve a director
Report only after the Board of Directors approves
Refer the matter to internal audit instead of PPATK
Wait until the director leaves the bank
bank.explanation: Article 15 gives the AML unit authority to report suspicious transactions directly to PPATK, including those by directors, commissioners or their affiliates.

bank.question: When may a bank file reports with PPATK on paper rather than through goAML?
options: Whenever the bank prefers, provided it calls PPATK first
For any report about a customer with fewer than three transactions
For all cash transaction reports below IDR 1 billion
Only in listed situations such as unavailable facilities, technical failure, force majeure or a PPATK system outage
bank.explanation: PPATK's guidance requires electronic filing through goAML and allows non-electronic filing only in the listed circumstances.

bank.question: A bank decides to postpone a suspicious transaction on its own initiative. What is the longest the postponement can last under Law 8/2010?
options: Three working days
Five working days
Thirty working days
Until PPATK finishes its analysis
bank.explanation: Article 26 allows postponement for up to five working days; by the fifth working day the bank decides whether to carry out or refuse the transaction.

bank.question: For how long must a bank keep records of a customer's identity documents after the relationship ends?
options: At least five years
At least three years
At least ten years
Until the next OJK inspection
bank.explanation: Law 8/2010 Article 21 and POJK 8/2023 Article 63 both set a minimum of five years after the relationship ends.

bank.question: In December 2023 OJK said it had ordered banks to block over 4,000 online gambling accounts. What else did it ask banks to do?
options: Stop opening accounts for anyone under 30
Report every e-wallet top-up to OJK
Strengthen CDD and EDD and build systems to profile and spot gambling activity
Close all accounts receiving transfers from e-wallets
bank.explanation: OJK's press release SP 190/OJK/GKPB/XII/2023 asked banks to develop profiling systems, strengthen CDD and EDD, and report off-profile transactions to PPATK as LTKMs.

bank.question: Why does reporting an LTKM not breach bank secrecy?
options: Because the customer consents in the account terms
Law 8/2010 exempts reporting duties from the secrecy rules binding the reporting party
Because OJK approves each report in advance
Because PPATK is part of the bank's own group
bank.explanation: Article 28 of Law 8/2010 says carrying out the reporting duty is exempt from the secrecy provisions that apply to the reporting party.

bank.question: Ahmad collects donations from friends, knowing part of the money will buy equipment for a terrorist group. He never touches a weapon. Under Law 9/2013, has he committed terrorism financing?
options: No; only those who carry out attacks commit an offence
Yes; collecting funds intended even partly for a terrorist organisation is the offence
No; the offence requires funds above IDR 100 million
Only if the group is also on a UN list
bank.explanation: Article 4 covers deliberately providing, collecting, giving or lending funds intended to be used wholly or partly for terrorism, a terrorist organisation or a terrorist. No amount or UN listing is required.

bank.question: A bank receives the DTTOT on 3 March (a working day). By when must it send the freeze report or nil report?
options: Within fourteen working days of receiving the list
Within twenty-four hours of receiving the list
Within three working days of receiving the list
Before the end of the month
bank.explanation: POJK 8/2023 sets three working days from receipt of the DTTOT or DPPSPM for freeze reports and nil reports.

bank.question: Screening of a corporate customer finds that its beneficial owner matches the DTTOT. What does POJK 8/2023 require?
options: Freeze immediately the funds the beneficial owner owns or controls, and report
Freeze nothing, because the account belongs to the company
Ask the company to replace the owner within 30 days
Close the account and return the balance to the company
bank.explanation: Article 53 requires an immediate freeze where the customer or beneficial owner matches, covering funds owned or controlled directly or indirectly, followed by freeze and LTKM reports.

bank.question: A listed customer's lawyer asks the bank to release funds to pay for the customer's food and medicine. Where can this request lawfully be handled?
options: By the branch manager, if the amount is small
Through the official DTTOT process, which provides an exception for basic necessities
By the bank's AML unit on its own authority
It cannot be handled; no exceptions exist
bank.explanation: PPATK's DTTOT page describes an exception for basic necessities within the official process. A branch or AML unit cannot lift a freeze on its own authority.

bank.question: A customer's screening alert shows the same common name as a DTTOT entry, but a different date of birth, nationality and ID number. What is the sound response?
options: Freeze the account immediately just in case
Tell the customer about the match and ask for comments
Clear it as a false positive and record the reasons
Ignore the alert without recording anything
bank.explanation: POJK 8/2023 requires banks to manage false positives and false negatives. With several identifiers clearly different, the bank clears the alert and documents why.

bank.question: Who notifies a person in writing that he has been placed on the DTTOT, and within what time?
options: The bank, within three working days
PPATK, within twenty-four hours
The police chief, within ten working days
OJK, within thirty days
bank.explanation: Article 27(7) of Law 9/2013 requires the police chief to notify the listed person or corporation in writing within ten working days.

bank.question: What must a commercial bank do before offering cross-border correspondent banking to a foreign respondent bank?
options: Understand the respondent's business, reputation and its home country's AML/CFT/CPF regime
Get PPATK's written approval of the respondent
Check only that the respondent has a SWIFT code
Ask the respondent's customers for their identity documents
bank.explanation: Article 54 of POJK 8/2023 requires the bank to gather this information before providing cross-border correspondent banking services.

bank.question: Besides screening names, POJK 8/2023 asks banks to manage another list-related risk. Which one?
options: Currency exchange risk on frozen balances
The reputational risk of publishing the lists
Sanction evasion by customers, walk-in customers or beneficial owners
Interest rate risk on frozen deposits
bank.explanation: Article 53(11) requires banks to identify, assess, understand and mitigate the risk of sanction evasion relating to the DTTOT and DPPSPM.

bank.question: Which duty does POJK 8/2023 place on the Board of Directors rather than the Board of Commissioners?
options: Approving the AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures
Ensuring officers and staff, especially relevant units and new joiners, attend yearly training
Evaluating the policies and overseeing the directors
Supervising how the directors carry out their duties
bank.explanation: Article 8(1)(f) makes the directors ensure yearly training. Approving, evaluating and overseeing are commissioners' duties under Article 9.

bank.question: What does POJK 8/2023 require the bank's individual risk assessment to refer to?
options: The bank's marketing plan for the year
The previous year's LTKM count only
The risk assessments of competitor banks
Indonesia's national and sectoral ML/TF/PF risk assessments
bank.explanation: Article 4(4) requires the bank's assessment to refer to Indonesia's national and sectoral risk assessments.

bank.question: When must a bank assess the ML/TF/PF risk of a new product or new technology under POJK 8/2023?
options: Before the product or technology is launched or used
Within six months after launch
At the next yearly risk assessment
Only if OJK asks for it
bank.explanation: Article 18 requires the risk assessment before new products, business practices, delivery mechanisms or technologies are launched or used.

bank.question: A commercial bank submits a required report to OJK 35 working days after the deadline. How does POJK 8/2023 treat it?
options: As not submitted, with a fine of IDR 10 million for that report
As late, with a fine of IDR 100,000 per day without limit
As on time, because it was eventually submitted
As late, with a fine capped at IDR 3 million
bank.explanation: Article 78 treats reports more than 30 working days late as not submitted. For commercial banks the fine is IDR 10 million per report, and the bank must still submit it.

bank.question: Which is evidence of an effective and independent internal control system under POJK 8/2023?
options: A larger number of LTKMs than last year
Independent examination to make sure the programme is effective
Approval of every account by the AML unit
Annual sign-off by the external auditor on financial statements only
bank.explanation: Article 65 points to adequate policies, procedures and internal monitoring, clear limits of authority, and independent examination of the programme's effectiveness.

bank.question: What must a bank's management information system maintain for every customer under POJK 8/2023?
options: A separate file for each account the customer holds
A single customer identification file
A copy of the customer's tax return
A record of the customer's social media accounts
bank.explanation: Article 69 requires a single customer identification file containing at least the identification data set out in the regulation.

bank.question: OJK fines a commercial bank under POJK 8/2023, but the bank made a loss the previous year. What happens to the fine calculation?
options: It is cancelled permanently
It is replaced by a fixed IDR 5 billion fine
It is doubled the following year
It is deferred until the bank makes a profit
bank.explanation: Article 80 defers the calculation of fines for institutions that made a loss in the previous year, and sets it on the profit once the bank is profitable again.

bank.question: Who, by law, is responsible for making sure a financial conglomerate applies the programme across all its offices and subsidiaries at home and abroad?
options: The financial institution that is the conglomerate's parent
Each subsidiary separately, with no group role
PPATK, through its foreign cooperation
The host country regulator only
bank.explanation: Article 67(3) makes the parent of the financial conglomerate responsible for group-wide application, including risk assessment and mitigation in each member.
